notes: General Linguistics major. 12 upper-division courses plus the undergraduate language requirement. Verified against the live catalog page.

buckets.label: Undergraduate language requirement (non-English language proficiency)
buckets.note: Proficiency in a non-English natural language, demonstrated by exam, coursework, or AP. Not tied to a fixed course set. Confirmed at catalog.ucsd.edu/curric/LING-ug.html. Not a fixed course set. All Linguistics majors demonstrate proficiency in ONE non-English natural language via any of three methods: (1) pass the Department of Linguistics reading proficiency exam + oral interview (offered in French, German, Italian, Russian, Spanish, Arabic, Farsi, Tagalog, Portuguese, Vietnamese, ASL, and possibly others); (2) complete a UC San Diego course representing the fourth quarter (or beyond) of instruction in a single non-English natural language with grade C- or better; or (3) score 4+ on an AP exam in a non-English language. Native speakers of a non-English language may petition to have English satisfy the requirement. Coursework path is satisfied by a 4th-quarter-level (typically the '2A'/second-year-entry) course in any language subject (e.g., LTFR/LTGM/LTSP/LTIT/LTRU/LTCH/CHIN/JAPN etc.), not a single fixed list, so type is proficiency rather than courses.

buckets.note: One course from each of THREE of the four areas. Areas: Computational Linguistics (117, 165, 167, 168, 169); Crosslinguistic Variation (108, 139, 141, 142, 143, 148, 152, 177); Language and Cognition (119, 148, 154, 155, 170, 171, 179, 180, 181); Language and Society (105, 146, 174, 175, 176, 177, 178). Course pool is the union of all four areas; distribution across three distinct areas is required.
